outcome: Maternal metabolic parameters (glucose and insulin levels in OGTT, fasting plasma glucose, HbA1c, lipid profile, prepregnancy BMI, gestational weight gain, chronic diseases)
Pregnancy outcomes (gestational hypertension, pre-eclampsia, eclampsia, time of delivery, mode of delivery)
Fetal parameters (weight and length at birth, ponderal index, neonatal complications, large for gestational age)
cohort: The study involved 60 women diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), with 20 also having celiac disease and 40 without celiac disease.
finding: Celiac women with GDM, compared to nonceliac women with GDM, had significantly lower blood glucose levels at 120' in OGTT, prepartum cLDL, and total cholesterol, and gave birth to children with significantly higher birth weight, ponderal index, and a higher likelihood of being large for gestational age.
mod_finding: N/A (mode of delivery was recorded but no significant difference was reported as a primary finding).
followup_time: N/A (outcomes measured at birth or during pregnancy)
cross-section timing: Outcomes measured during pregnancy and at the time of birth.
birth_weight: Not restricted by specific weight; birth weight and ponderal index were measured outcomes.
gest_age: Not restricted by specific gestational age; 'large for gestational age' was a measured outcome.
